method: Whitespace is removed from a sequence of at most 96 binary digits, which must form complete groups for the selected scheme. BPSK maps 0 and 1 to -1 and +1 on the I axis. QPSK uses 00, 01, 11 and 10 counter-clockwise from the positive I, positive Q quadrant, with each coordinate divided by sqrt(2). 8-PSK uses the cyclic Gray sequence 000, 001, 011, 010, 110, 111, 101 and 100 at 45-degree intervals starting on the positive I axis. Square QAM independently maps the first half of each label to I and the second half to Q using reflected Gray level sequences: 00, 01, 11, 10 select -3, -1, +1, +3 divided by sqrt(10) for 16-QAM; 000, 001, 011, 010, 110, 111, 101, 100 select -7, -5, -3, -1, +1, +3, +5, +7 divided by sqrt(42) for 64-QAM. Each full constellation therefore has unit average power. Coordinates are copied to four decimal places; calculations retain full precision. This is an educational mapping reference, not a modem configuration or link-performance calculator.
